resources.string: Would rather: would prefer to
Not: do, does or did + not makes a verb negative (at the start: don’t do it)
Question: do, does or did comes before the subject
Let’s: a suggestion to do something together
Would like: a polite way to say want (Would you like…? offers something)
Want to: wish to do something (wanna in casual speech)
Can: be able to, or be allowed to
Present continuous: happening now, or a fixed plan
There is / there are: something exists or is in a place
Like, love or hate + -ing: how you feel about an activity
A lot of: many or much (everyday English)
How many: the number (things you can count); how much: the amount or price
To + verb: the infinitive (says why, or follows want, need, hope…)
Be in the present: am (I), is (he, she, it), are (you, we, they)
Present simple with he, she or it: habits and facts
Past simple: a finished action or state in the past
A or an: one of many, or something mentioned for the first time (an before a vowel sound)
The: a specific thing both people know about
And: joins two words or ideas
But: introduces a contrast
Or: a choice between two things
Because: gives the reason (+ a sentence)
How often: always > usually > often > sometimes > rarely > never
’s: belongs to (Tom’s bag = the bag of Tom)
Too (at the end): also
Ago: back in time from now (two days ago)
In: inside; with months, years and parts of the day
On: on a surface; with days and dates
At: at a point or place; with clock times
To: toward a place or person (go to, give to)
For: the purpose or the receiver; for + a length of time
From: the starting point (place, time or origin)
With: together with; using (cut with a knife)
Of: belonging to, or part of (a cup of tea)
About: on the topic of; or roughly (about ten minutes)
Question word: asks for information (what, where, when, why, who, how)
Question: be or have comes before the subject
Imperative: the plain verb with no subject gives an order or a request
Don’t have to: it is not necessary (but you may)
Why don’t you / we…?: a friendly suggestion
Be going to: a plan, or something you can see is coming (gonna in speech)
Used to: a past habit or state that is no longer true
Have to: it is necessary (a rule or the situation); had to = past
Need to: it is necessary for you
Mustn’t: it is not allowed
Verb + to + verb: some verbs are followed by to (decide to, hope to, try to)
Past continuous: in progress at a moment in the past (often interrupted)
Have got: have or own (mostly British English)
Present perfect: happened before now and still matters (experience, result, up to now)
Will: the future, a quick decision, a promise or an offer
Could: was able to; a polite request; something possible
Must: it is necessary; or I am sure it is true
Should: advice, or what is right or expected
Comparative: more of a quality than something else
Superlative: more than all the others
Too + adjective: more than is good or possible
Enough: as much as needed (adjective + enough, enough + noun)
So + adjective: very (shows strong feeling)
So: and because of this (the result)
Before / after: earlier or later than something (+ noun, -ing or a sentence)
Until: up to a time, then it stops
Already: before now, or sooner than expected
Yet: until now (in questions and negatives)
Still: continuing, not finished
Just: a very short time ago; or only
Ever: at any time (Have you ever…?)
Some: in positive sentences and offers; any: in questions and negatives
Many: things you can count; much: amounts you can’t count
A few: a small number, some
Every / each: all of a group, one by one
No + noun: not any
-self: the same person as the subject (by myself = alone)
-ly: turns an adjective into an adverb (how something is done)
Phrasal verb: a verb + small word, often with a new meaning (give up = stop)
How about…? / What about…?: a suggestion (+ noun or -ing)
By: near; not later than; who did it (after a passive); how (by bus)
During: at some time in a period (during the night)
Without: not having or not doing (+ noun or -ing)
Into: moving to the inside
Between: in the space or time from one to the other
Both: the two together (both … and …)
If + present: a real possibility (… will happen)
When: at the time that
Present perfect continuous: started in the past and still going on (for, since)
Past perfect: happened before another past event
Future continuous: in progress at a time in the future
Passive after can, will, must…: (it can be done)
Passive: the subject receives the action (by + who did it)
Be able to: can (in any tense: will be able to)
Be supposed to: it is expected or planned (but often doesn’t happen)
Had better: strong advice (or there will be a problem)
Have got to (gotta): have to, must (informal)
Be used to: be familiar with it (get used to: become familiar)
Be about to: going to happen very soon
May: possibly; or polite permission (May I…?)
Might: perhaps (less sure than may)
Shall I / we…?: an offer or a suggestion
Would: an imagined situation, a polite request, or a past habit
Some verbs are followed by -ing (enjoy, finish, avoid, keep)
Verb + someone + to + verb: what you want, ask or tell someone to do
Let / make + someone + verb (no to): allow or force someone to do it
After a preposition (of, for, at…), a verb takes -ing
In order to: for the purpose of
So that: in order that (+ a sentence, often with can or could)
So / such … that: so much that there is a result
Because of + noun: for this reason
Although: there is a contrast (like but)
Even if: whether or not this happens
While: during the time that; or whereas (a contrast)
As soon as: immediately when
In case: because it might happen (be ready for it)
Whether: if (when there are two choices)
Unless: if not; except if
Since + a time: from then until now (with have done); or since = because
Instead of: in place of (+ noun or -ing)
Either … or: one or the other; neither … nor: not one and not the other
Wish + past: you want something to be different (wish + had done: regret)
After a comma, who or which adds extra information about the noun
Whose: of whom (the girl whose father…)
Relative clause: who (people), which (things) or that (both) tells you more about the noun before it
Reported speech: what someone said (tenses often move back: is → was)
That + sentence: what someone thinks, says or knows (often left out)
Look forward to (+ noun or -ing): be happy about something that is coming
Get + adjective: become (get tired, get better)
So do I / neither do I: me too (agreeing with what was said)
It is + adjective + to + verb: describes an action (It’s easy to learn)
Question tag: checks that the listener agrees (positive sentence → negative tag)
Such as: for example
According to: as said by a person or a source
However: but (starts a contrasting sentence)
-ness: makes a noun from an adjective (happy → happiness)
-ment: makes a noun from a verb (move → movement)
-tion / -sion: makes a noun from a verb (decide → decision)
-ful: full of (care → careful)
-less: without (home → homeless)
-able / -ible: can be done (wash → washable)
If + past: imagined or unlikely now (… would happen)
Past perfect continuous: had been going on until a moment in the past
Future perfect: will be finished by a time in the future
Perfect passive: has been done (by someone)
Continuous passive: is being done right now
Get + past participle: something happens to someone (get hurt, get married)
Should have done: it was right but didn’t happen (regret or criticism)
Could have done: it was possible but didn’t happen
Must have done: I am sure it happened
Might / may have done: perhaps it happened
Would have done: an imagined past result (if … had …)
Ought to: should (a little formal)
If only: a strong wish or regret
As if: as it would be if (it seems so, but may not be)
As long as: only if
Despite / in spite of + noun or -ing: although
Not only … but also: both, and the second is more surprising
Otherwise: if not (something bad will happen)
Therefore: so, for this reason (formal)
Due to: because of (formal)
-ever: any … at all; no matter what, who or where
If + had done: imagining a different past (… would have happened)
Negative word first, then the helper verb before the subject (formal, for emphasis)
Subjunctive: after suggest or insist that, the plain verb is used (he go, she be)
As … as: equal (not as … as: less)
This / these: near you (this one); that / those: farther away (that one)
Not: makes a word or a sentence negative (I’m not hungry, it isn’t far)
All: every one of a group, or the whole of something
Like: similar to, in the same way as (He looks like his father)
Place or movement: where something is, or which way it goes (under the table, across the road)
As: in the role of (works as a nurse); or because, while
